3844e3626f.fzText: Attendance is a fundamental requirement of this course. Since printmaking techniques are taught through in class demonstrations and studio practice, students are expected to attend every session. Regular attendance and active participation are essential to qualify for the final portfolio. Students who fail to meet the attendance requirement may not be eligible to submit the final portfolio.
weekly: Introduction to Serigraphy; Materials and shop safety. The course promotes environmental awareness through the reuse of everyday and discarded materials in printmaking practices. Students are encouraged to repurpose waste paper, newspapers, magazines, old T-shirts, cleaning cloths, and towels, reducing material waste while exploring sustainable approaches to printmaking

Work week: As part of this week’s activities, students will create original artworks using different techniques and possibilities of printmaking within the framework of the theme “LÖSEV: The Name of Miracles and Hope.” Students enrolled in the FA 467 Curatorial Studies course will select a group of works for exhibition, organize their placement and the overall exhibition design at FADA Gallery, and prepare the curatorial text for the exhibition. The exhibition will take place during the the first week of November at FADA Gallery. The project aims to bring together artistic production, curatorial practice, and social responsibility, encouraging students to engage with issues of social awareness and solidarity through their creative and curatorial work.
Critique and Intro to exposure unit

602a9ff33c.fzText: Students must have attended 70% of the classes. In order to qualify the course, the student must have submitted three assignments and attended off campus visits (museums&galleries)
weekly: Who is a Curator? What is a Curatorial Exhibition? An introduction to the role of the curator and the question of how ideas, artworks, artists and audiences come together to create an exhibition.
The Curator as Mediator; Understanding how curators connect artists, artworks, institutions and audiences.
Exhibition Concepts and Themes; Learning how curators develop a strong concept, narrative and thematic framework for an exhibition.

As part of this week’s activities, students will curate an exhibition featuring original artworks created by students in FA 213 Introduction to Printmaking (sections1,2,3) in response to the theme ‘LÖSEV: The Name of Miracles and Hope.’ FA 467 students will review and select works produced through different printmaking techniques and approaches, develop the exhibition concept and layout, organize the installation of the selected works at FADA Gallery, and prepare the curatorial text for the exhibition. The exhibition will take place during the first week of November. Trough this collaborative project, students will engage with artistic production, curatorial practice, and social responsibility, exploring the role of art and exhibition.
Museums, Galleries and Art Institutions; Comparing different institutional models and examining how curatorial decisions operate within them.
Biennials, Art Fairs and Independent Exhibitions; Examining large scale exhibitions, art fairs, biennials and alternative curatorial platforms.
Biennials, Art Fairs and Independent Exhibitions; Examining large scale exhibitions, art fairs, biennials and alternative curatorial platforms.
Space, Display and Installation; Understanding how architecture, space, lighting, scale and installation influence the viewer's experience.
Guest Curator: Curating in Practice; A guest curator visits the class to discuss their professional practice, curatorial experiences, exhibition making process and challenges in the field.

AI, Labor and Power; Who performs the invisible labor behind AI? How is technological power produced and in whose hands? How do artists participate in these systems while simultaneously making them visible and subjecting them to critique?
Developing a Curatorial Project; Students develop and present their own exhibition concept, including its theme, artists, artworks and spatial approach.
outcomes: have a command upon important terminology used in curation practices within a globalized curatorial discourse
